correctness.rationale: Diameter endpoints are extreme in Euclidean space. The source vertex theorem reduces every endpoint to a prefix of \(n,n-1,\ldots,1\). Coordinatewise, \((u_i-v_i)^2\le\max\{u_i^2,v_i^2\}\), so the total squared distance is bounded by the sum of at most \(m\) entries from two copies of the source square spectrum. Selecting the largest \(s=\min\{m,2n\}\) entries yields the formula, and disjoint prefix supports attain it. Strictness when both coordinates are positive, together with strict ordering of the positive squares, gives the complete equality classification.

value.rationale: Euclidean diameter is a standard metric invariant complementary to the face, volume, Ehrhart, and inradius data already studied for partial permutohedra. The theorem covers the full two-parameter family, gives all equality pairs, and reveals a sharp structural threshold: once \(m=2n\), the two endpoints can place all \(n\) allowed positive values on disjoint supports and the diameter thereafter becomes independent of dimension. The result also applies immediately to the parking-function specialization by translation, while remaining realization-sensitive rather than a graph-metric restatement.
